docs.title: Neighborhood Module API Reference
docs.text:
See Atera breast cancer neighborhoods for hextile niches and alpha-shape comparisons, and pancreas islet gradients for a complete gradient-analysis and NeighborhoodCollection workflow.

Neighborhoods are GeoDataFrames with one row per neighborhood and an id column (name by default, falling back to neighborhood_id / nbhd_id). They come from alpha shapes, hextiles, gradient rings, or your own polygons, and are summarized against cell-level AnnData or MuData into new neighborhood-level AnnData objects:

import celldega as dega

gdf_hex = dega.nbhd.generate_hextile(adata, diameter=100)

# neighborhoods x genes (mean expression of the cells inside each hexagon)
adata_nbg = dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_by_gene(gdf_hex, "cell", adata)

# neighborhoods x cell types (proportions)
adata_nbp = dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_by_pop(adata, gdf_hex, category="leiden")

# neighborhoods x neighborhoods relations (e.g. between cluster alpha shapes)
gdf_alpha = dega.nbhd.alpha_shape_cell_clusters(adata, cat="leiden", alphas=[150])
gdf_alpha = dega.nbhd.filter_alpha_shapes(gdf_alpha, alpha=150)
adata_overlap = dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_overlap(gdf_alpha, metric="iou")

# every result is ready for a Clustergram
mat = dega.clust.Matrix(adata_nbp)

With a MuData (e.g. RNA + protein), calc_nbhd_by_gene aggregates every modality and returns a MuData of neighborhood-level modalities; pass modality= to aggregate just one. In the calc_nbhd_* functions and calc_gradient, any object exposing to_geodataframe() can stand in for the neighborhood GeoDataFrame.

alpha_shape returns Shapely geometry and calc_gradient returns a GeoDataFrame of rings. With coordinates in microns:

footprint = dega.nbhd.alpha_shape(adata.obsm["spatial"][seed_mask], inv_alpha=40)
rings = dega.nbhd.calc_gradient(
    footprint, direction="both", bin_width=25, max_dist=200,
    clip_reference=adata,
)
adata_rings = dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_by_pop(adata, rings, category="leiden", min_cells=1)

Multiple footprints are unioned before buffering. Cells are assigned to rings with a within spatial join, so a cell lying exactly on a ring boundary is not counted in either ring.

docs.title: Storing results in a NeighborhoodCollection
docs.text:
NeighborhoodCollection is a MuData-backed container that keeps neighborhood geometry, per-neighborhood modalities, and neighborhood-by-neighborhood relations aligned on one observation axis. It stores data only: pass it to the functions above in place of the GeoDataFrame, then store what they return.

nc = dega.nbhd.NeighborhoodCollection(gdf=gdf_alpha, nbhd_type="alpha_shape")

pop = dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_by_pop(adata, nc, category="leiden", min_cells=5)
nc.subset(pop.obs_names)             # optional: drop neighborhoods below min_cells
nc.add_mod("population", pop)
nc.add_mod("gene", dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_by_gene(nc, adata=adata))
nc.add_relation("overlap", dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_overlap(nc, metric="iou"))

trx = dega.nbhd.read_transcripts(data_dir)
nc.obs = nc.obs.join(dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_transcript_assignment(nc, trx))

mat = dega.clust.Matrix(mdata=nc, color_by="population")

Neighborhood generation and calculation.

Neighborhoods are GeoDataFrame objects (one row per neighborhood) built from cells (alpha shapes, hextiles, gradient rings) and summarized against cell-level AnnData/MuData into new neighborhood-level AnnData.

docs.title: NeighborhoodCollection
docs.text:
Bases: CelldegaCollection

Neighborhood-level or spatial-region MuData collection.

Observations are neighborhoods or spatial regions. Feature modalities live in mod and global observation relations live in relations/mdata.obsp. Geometry is kept as a live GeoDataFrame in memory; durable geometry storage can be layered on later with WKB columns or GeoParquet sidecars.

The collection only stores data. Computation lives in celldega.nbhd functions, which accept the collection wherever they take a neighborhood GeoDataFrame and return plain objects to store back::

nc = NeighborhoodCollection(gdf=gdf_alpha)
pop = dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_by_pop(adata, nc, category="leiden")
nc.subset(pop.obs_names)  # optional: drop neighborhoods below min_cells
nc.add_mod("population", pop)
nc.add_mod("gene", dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_by_gene(nc, adata=adata))
nc.add_relation("overlap", dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_overlap(nc))
rings = NeighborhoodCollection(
    gdf=dega.nbhd.calc_gradient(nc.gdf.loc[["9"]]), nbhd_type="gradient"
)

For a MuData, cat is looked up in the global obs and then in the modalities' own obs. cat : str Column with cluster/category labels. alphas : Sequence[float] Inverse alpha values to compute shapes for. meta_cluster : pd.DataFrame | None Optional cluster metadata with a 'color' column, indexed by cluster. If not provided, colors come from uns[f'{cat}_colors'] when available, otherwise default to black. modality : str, optional For a MuData input, the modality to take coordinates and labels from. spatial_key : str, default "spatial" Key of the cell coordinates in obsm.

docs.title: alpha_shape_cell_clusters_by_slice(adata, cluster_attr='cluster', slice_attr='slice_id', z_attr=None, alphas=(150,), meta_cluster=None, z_jitter=0.1, progress_every=0, *, modality=None, spatial_key='spatial')
docs.text:
Compute one alpha shape per (slice, cluster) pair, each stamped with its slice's Z.

For each slice, computes alpha_shape_cell_clusters / filter_alpha_shapes at a single alpha resolution, then stamps every resulting polygon with that slice's Z (from z_attr, or 0.0 if not given) plus a small per-cluster jitter (via stamp_z) so overlapping, coplanar cluster polygons within a slice don't z-fight.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: adata : AnnData or MuData Cell-level data with spatial coordinates in obsm[spatial_key] and cluster_attr / slice_attr (and, if given, z_attr) columns in obs. cluster_attr : str Column with cluster/category labels. slice_attr : str Column identifying each slice. z_attr : str | None Column with each cell's Z coordinate (expected to be one constant value per slice). If None, every slice is stamped at Z=0. alphas : Sequence[float] Must contain exactly one inverse-alpha resolution (see alpha_shape) — this function computes a single resolution per (slice, cluster), unlike alpha_shape_cell_clusters which can sweep several. meta_cluster : pd.DataFrame | None Optional cluster metadata with a 'color' column. Defaults to the colors in uns[f"{cluster_attr}_colors"], or a distinct fallback palette when none are stored, so every slice shares one palette. z_jitter : float Per-cluster Z offset within a slice, to avoid z-fighting between coplanar cluster polygons that would otherwise sit at the exact same Z. progress_every : int Print a progress line every this many slices processed (0, the default, disables it). Each alpha shape involves a Delaunay triangulation plus verification, so this is the slow part of a neighborhood-cloud pre-processing run on a dataset with many slices. modality : str, optional For a MuData input, the modality to take coordinates and labels from. spatial_key : str, default "spatial" Key of the cell coordinates in obsm.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: gpd.GeoDataFrame One row per (slice, cluster) neighborhood, with columns name (f"{slice_id}__{cluster_id}"), cluster_id, slice_id, geometry (3D), color, area, inv_alpha, cell_count.

docs.title: calc_gradient(source, direction='both', bin_width=10, max_dist=50, *, technology=None, scale_um_per_pixel=None, is_pixel_space=False, clip_boundary=None, clip_reference=None, clip_alpha=100, add_colors=True, nbhd_col='name')
docs.text:
Generate gradient bands around a region of interest as a GeoDataFrame.

Starting from the boundary of the merged source geometry, this builds fixed-width bands every bin_width microns out to max_dist:

  • Outward bands grow away from the ROI (positive distance). Use clip_boundary/clip_reference to stop them from running off the tissue.
  • Inward bands erode into the ROI (negative distance) and stop automatically once the geometry erodes to nothing.

Each band is one row of the returned GeoDataFrame, ordered inner-most to outer-most, with a signed distance so you can spatially join cells to bands (gpd.sjoin) and correlate composition or expression against distance from the ROI edge.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default source GeoDataFrame | GeoSeries | BaseGeometry | Any

The ROI. May be a GeoDataFrame/GeoSeries (all rows are dissolved into one shape), a bare shapely (Multi)Polygon, or a neighborhood-like object exposing to_geodataframe().

required direction str

"outward", "inward", or "both" (default).

'both' bin_width float

Width of each ring in microns (default 10).

10 max_dist float

Maximum distance from the ROI boundary in microns (default 50). Applied symmetrically to outward and inward bands.

50 technology str | None

Imaging platform (e.g. "Xenium") used to look up scale_um_per_pixel when the geometry is in pixel space. Ignored if scale_um_per_pixel is given.

None scale_um_per_pixel float | None

Microns per pixel. Required (directly or via technology) when is_pixel_space=True.

None is_pixel_space bool

True if source geometry is in pixel units; False (default) if it is already in microns. Controls how micron ring widths are converted to the geometry's units and how areas are reported.

False clip_boundary Any | None

Optional precomputed tissue boundary (GeoDataFrame/GeoSeries/geometry) to clip outward rings to. Takes precedence over clip_reference. Use this to pass your own whole-tissue alpha shape at an alpha of your choosing.

None clip_reference Any | None

Optional source of cell positions from which a tissue alpha shape is computed on the fly to clip outward rings. Accepts an AnnData (uses obsm["spatial"] or x/y centroid obs columns), a GeoDataFrame/GeoSeries of cells, or an (N, 2) array. Must be in the same coordinate space as source.

None clip_alpha float

Inverse-alpha value for the on-the-fly alpha shape (default 100). Larger values trace tissue boundaries more loosely.

100 add_colors bool

If True (default), add a color column (Blues for outward bands, Reds for inward) for visualization.

True nbhd_col str

Name of the band-identifier column in the output (default "name"), matching the neighborhood functions' default nbhd_col.

'name'

Returns:

Type Description GeoDataFrame

A GeoDataFrame with one row per ring, ordered inner-most to

GeoDataFrame

outer-most, and columns:

GeoDataFrame
  • name / ring_range_um — band label, e.g. "out (+0~+10) µm".
GeoDataFrame
  • direction — "outward" or "inward".
GeoDataFrame
  • dist_start_um / dist_end_um — signed band edges in microns.
GeoDataFrame
  • area / area_um2 / area_px2 — band areas.
GeoDataFrame
  • color — hex color (when add_colors).
GeoDataFrame
  • geometry — the band polygon, in the source coordinate space.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If direction is invalid, or is_pixel_space=True without a resolvable scale_um_per_pixel.

Examples:

Build bands from an alpha-shape GeoDataFrame in micron coordinates::

>>> rings = dega.nbhd.calc_gradient(
...     footprints, direction="both", bin_width=25, max_dist=200,
...     clip_reference=adata,
... )

adata.obsm["spatial"] supplies tissue coordinates for clipping. Multiple footprints are unioned before buffering, so adjacent regions do not produce overlapping band interiors. Shared band boundaries still require a tie-breaking rule when assigning cells with gpd.sjoin.

docs.title: calc_nbhd_bordering(gdf_nbhd, metric='border_ratio', nbhd_col='name', category='leiden')
docs.text: Calculate pairwise border relationships between neighborhoods.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: gdf_nbhd : GeoDataFrame or neighborhood-like object Neighborhood geometries with an identifier column (nbhd_col). metric : str, default "border_ratio" The border metric to compute: - "border_ratio": shared border length over the row neighborhood's perimeter (asymmetric). - "border_length": raw shared border length (symmetric). - "binary": 1 if the neighborhoods touch, 0 otherwise (symmetric). nbhd_col : str, default "name" Column with neighborhood identifiers. category : str, default "leiden" Name of the category the neighborhoods represent (e.g. "leiden"); used for the category column in obs/var and the colors in uns.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: AnnData Square neighborhoods x neighborhoods matrix with obs["perimeter"], uns["metric"], and the neighborhood category/colors when the geometry has cat/color columns.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Shared border length is the length of the intersection of the two neighborhood boundaries, so this suits neighborhoods that touch without overlapping. For overlapping neighborhoods use calc_nbhd_overlap.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: adata_border = dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_bordering(gdf_hex_niche) mat = dega.clust.Matrix(adata_border)

docs.title: calc_nbhd_by_gene(gdf_nbhd, by='cell', adata=None, data_dir=None, nbhd_col='name', min_cells=1, *, include_variance=False, modality=None, layer=None, feature_type=None, spatial_key='spatial', gdf_trx=None)
docs.text:
Calculate a neighborhood-by-gene expression matrix.

Computes gene expression for each neighborhood, either from cell-level expression (mean expression of the cells within each neighborhood) or from raw transcript counts (cell-free mode).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: gdf_nbhd : GeoDataFrame or neighborhood-like object Neighborhood geometries with an identifier column (nbhd_col). Objects exposing to_geodataframe() are accepted too. by : str, default "cell" - "cell": mean expression of cells within each neighborhood (requires adata) - "cell-free": transcript counts within each neighborhood (requires gdf_trx or data_dir) adata : AnnData or MuData, optional Cell-level data with spatial coordinates in obsm[spatial_key]. Required when by="cell". For a MuData, every modality is aggregated (one output modality per input modality) unless modality is given. data_dir : str, optional Directory containing transcripts.parquet, used for by="cell-free" when gdf_trx is not given. nbhd_col : str, default "name" Column in gdf_nbhd with neighborhood identifiers (falls back to neighborhood_id/nbhd_id). min_cells : int, default 1 Minimum cells (or, for by="cell-free", transcripts) a neighborhood needs to be included. With by="cell", neighborhoods without any cells are never included. include_variance : bool, default False With by="cell", also store per-neighborhood, per-gene variance (population variance) in layers["variance"]. modality : str, optional For a MuData input, aggregate only this modality and return an AnnData. layer : str, optional Aggregate this layer instead of X. feature_type : str, optional Entity type of the features (written to var["entity_type"] and uns["axis_entities"]). Defaults to "gene" for AnnData and gene-like modalities (rna, gene, expression), else the modality name. spatial_key : str, default "spatial" Key of the cell coordinates in obsm. gdf_trx : GeoDataFrame, optional Transcript points with a feature_name column (see read_transcripts), for by="cell-free".

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: AnnData or MuData Neighborhoods x features, with obs["n_cells"] (or obs["n_transcripts"]), uns["by"], uns["axis_entities"], and the neighborhood cat/color columns when the geometry has them. A MuData input without modality returns a MuData with one modality per input modality.

docs.title: calc_nbhd_by_pop(adata, gdf_nbhd, category='leiden', nbhd_col='name', min_cells=5, output='proportion', *, modality=None, spatial_key='spatial')
docs.text:
Calculate the cell population distribution of each neighborhood.

Computes a neighborhood-by-population matrix showing the distribution of cell categories (e.g., clusters, cell types) within each neighborhood.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: adata : AnnData or MuData Cell-level data with spatial coordinates in obsm[spatial_key] and the category column in obs. For a MuData, category is looked up in the global obs (also as "<modality>:<category>") and then in the modalities' own obs. gdf_nbhd : GeoDataFrame or neighborhood-like object Neighborhood geometries with an identifier column (nbhd_col). category : str, default "leiden" Cell category column (e.g. "leiden", "cell_type"). nbhd_col : str, default "name" Column in gdf_nbhd with neighborhood identifiers. min_cells : int, default 5 Minimum number of cells a neighborhood needs to be included. output : str, default "proportion" - "proportion": fraction of cells per category (sums to 1 per neighborhood) - "counts": raw cell counts per category modality : str, optional For a MuData input, the modality to take coordinates and category from. spatial_key : str, default "spatial" Key of the cell coordinates in obsm.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: AnnData Neighborhoods x categories with obs["n_cells"], uns["category"], uns["output"], var["entity_type"] = "cell_population", and category colors (var["color"], uns[f"{category}_colors"]) when the cell data has them.

docs.title: calc_nbhd_overlap(gdf_nbhd, metric='iou', nbhd_col='name', category='leiden')
docs.text: Calculate pairwise overlap between all neighborhoods.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: gdf_nbhd : GeoDataFrame or neighborhood-like object Neighborhood geometries with an identifier column (nbhd_col). metric : str, default "iou" The overlap metric to compute: - "iou": intersection over union; symmetric, from 0 (no overlap) to 1 (identical geometries). - "ioa": intersection over the row neighborhood's area; asymmetric, useful for containment analysis. - "intersection": raw intersection area in square units. nbhd_col : str, default "name" Column with neighborhood identifiers. category : str, default "leiden" Name of the category the neighborhoods represent (e.g. "leiden"); used for the category column in obs/var and the colors in uns.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: AnnData Square neighborhoods x neighborhoods matrix with obs["area"], uns["metric"], and the neighborhood category/colors when the geometry has cat/color columns.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: adata_iou = dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_overlap(gdf_alpha, metric="iou") mat = dega.clust.Matrix(adata_iou)

docs.title: calc_nbhd_transcript_assignment(gdf_nbhd, gdf_trx=None, *, data_dir=None, nbhd_col='name')
docs.text:
Per-neighborhood transcript counts and cell-assignment proportion.

A transcript counts as assigned when its cell_id is not "UNASSIGNED".

Assumption: transcript-to-cell assignment is not computed here — it must already be present in the instrument data, with unassigned transcripts marked by the "UNASSIGNED" sentinel (Xenium convention). A missing cell_id column raises ValueError; a complete absence of the sentinel warns (it may be genuinely fully assigned, or use a different convention).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: gdf_nbhd : GeoDataFrame or neighborhood-like object Neighborhood geometries with an identifier column (nbhd_col). gdf_trx : GeoDataFrame, optional Transcript points with a cell_id column (see read_transcripts). data_dir : str, optional Directory containing transcripts.parquet, used when gdf_trx is not given. nbhd_col : str, default "name" Column in gdf_nbhd with neighborhood identifiers.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: pd.DataFrame Indexed by neighborhood id with columns total_transcripts, unassigned_transcripts, and transcript_assignment_proportion (assigned / total; 0.0 when a neighborhood has no transcripts).

docs.title: filter_alpha_shapes(gdf_alpha, alpha, min_area=0, clean_names=True)
docs.text:
Filter alpha shapes by a specific alpha value and optionally clean up names.

Alpha shapes computed by alpha_shape_cell_clusters have names in the format {category}_{alpha} (e.g., "cluster_0_150"). This function filters to a specific alpha value and removes the trailing _{alpha} suffix from names.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: gdf_alpha : gpd.GeoDataFrame GeoDataFrame of alpha shapes with 'inv_alpha', 'area', 'name', and 'cat' columns. Typically the output of alpha_shape_cell_clusters. alpha : float The inverse alpha value to filter for (must match values in 'inv_alpha' column). min_area : float, default 0 Minimum area threshold. Shapes with area <= min_area are excluded. clean_names : bool, default True If True, removes the trailing _{alpha} suffix from the 'name' column, leaving just the category name (e.g., "cluster_0" instead of "cluster_0_150").

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: gpd.GeoDataFrame Filtered GeoDataFrame with optionally cleaned names.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: gdf_alpha = dega.nbhd.alpha_shape_cell_clusters(adata, cat="leiden") gdf_filtered = dega.nbhd.filter_alpha_shapes(gdf_alpha, alpha=150)

docs.title: Names are now just category names without the alpha suffix
docs.text: print(gdf_filtered["name"].tolist()[:3]) ['0', '1', '2']

docs.title: hextile_niche(gdf_hex, adata_hex, category='leiden', dissolve=True)
docs.text:
Create niche polygons from hextiles based on clustering results.

Takes hexagon geometries and assigns them to niches based on clustering (e.g., Leiden clustering of hexagon population distributions). Optionally dissolves adjacent hexagons of the same niche into unified polygons.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: gdf_hex : gpd.GeoDataFrame GeoDataFrame of hexagon geometries. Must be indexed by hexagon name (matching adata_hex.obs.index). adata_hex : AnnData or MuData Hexagon-level data containing clustering results in obs[category]. The index must match the hexagon names in gdf_hex. Colors can be provided in uns[f"{category}_colors"]. category : str, default "leiden" Column name in adata_hex.obs containing the niche/cluster assignment. dissolve : bool, default True If True, dissolve adjacent hexagons of the same niche into unified MultiPolygon geometries. If False, return individual hexagons with their niche assignment.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: gpd.GeoDataFrame If dissolve=True: GeoDataFrame with dissolved niche polygons. Columns: "name", "cat", "geometry", "color", "area". If dissolve=False: GeoDataFrame with individual hexagons and niche assignment. Columns: "name", "cat", "geometry", "color".

docs.title: Generate hexagons and compute population distribution
docs.text: gdf_hex = dega.nbhd.generate_hextile(adata, diameter=100) adata_hex = dega.nbhd.calc_nbhd_by_pop(adata, gdf_hex, category="leiden")

docs.title: Cluster hexagons by population similarity (e.g., using scanpy)
docs.text: import scanpy as sc sc.pp.pca(adata_hex) sc.pp.neighbors(adata_hex) sc.tl.leiden(adata_hex)

docs.title: Create dissolved niche polygons
docs.text: gdf_niche = dega.nbhd.hextile_niche(gdf_hex, adata_hex, category="leiden")

docs.title: Or keep individual hexagons with niche assignment
docs.text: gdf_hex_niche = dega.nbhd.hextile_niche(gdf_hex, adata_hex, dissolve=False)

docs.title: stamp_z(geometry, z)
docs.text:
Stamp a constant Z onto every vertex of a 2D geometry.

Used to place a 2D alpha-shape polygon (or any other geometry) at a fixed height in a 3D scene, e.g. one alpha shape per (slice, cluster) placed at its slice's Z coordinate. Any desired per-geometry offset (e.g. a small jitter to avoid z-fighting between coplanar overlapping polygons within a slice) should already be folded into z.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: geometry : Shapely geometry object (e.g., Polygon, MultiPolygon), or None. z : float Constant Z value to assign to every vertex.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Shapely geometry with a Z ordinate on every vertex, or None.

docs.title: Pre Module API Reference
docs.text:
Prepare instrument output for Landscape with the DegaFiles preparation and hosting guide. Examples include Atera preprocessing and custom segmentation.

See Add aligned H&E to DegaFiles for importing an optional histology background into Landscape and Yearbook.

For CellCloud, use write_point_cloud_dataset for compact indexed Parquet DegaFiles or write_point_cloud_zarr for an AnnData Zarr with sparse CSC expression. Both support rounded XYZ positions and named alignments; see the CellCloud preparation examples and mouse-brain workflow.

Module for pre-processing to generate LandscapeFiles from ST data.

docs.title: add_aligned_he(path_dega_files, image_path, *, alignment=None)
docs.text:
Tile H&E in the existing image coordinate system and register it in the manifest.

Run after pre.main() or on an existing DegaFiles directory. Without alignment, the RGB image must already have exactly the reference image's width, height, origin and pixel scale. No alignment is estimated here.

alignment may be a 3x3 array or a headerless CSV path. It maps H&E pixel coordinates to the existing DegaFiles image pixels: [x, y, 1] (column vectors). Xenium Explorer imagealignment.csv files use this convention. Translation, rotation, reflection, shear and scale are supported. The image is resampled onto the reference canvas; outside pixels are white.

Existing fluorescence, cells and transcripts are preserved. The new pyramid uses WebP and the reference tile size, with Parquet packing when DegaFiles use row groups. Requires the optional celldega[pre] dependency and libvips. An existing H&E pyramid is never overwritten. Returns the H&E manifest entry.

If provided, files will be saved as cell_clusters_{segmentation_name}/. If None, files are saved to the default cell_clusters/ directory.

docs.text:

docs.title: write_gene_cell_scatter(adata, gene_list, path_dega_files, slice_attr='slice_id', z_attr=None, min_expression=2.0, min_cells=4, max_cells=50000, progress_every=500)
docs.text:
Gene-coloring writer: a capped, top-expressing cell scatter per gene.

Selects each gene's top-expressing cells (_select_top_expressing_cells, an O(n) argpartition, no geometry at all), so "browse any gene" scales to a large gene list: a capped point scatter of real single-cell positions and expression values, colored by per-cell expression.

Reads each gene's expression directly from an already-loaded adata.X column.

Writes nbhd_cloud/cells/by_gene/<gene>.parquet (columns: cell_id, gene, slice_id, x, y, z, expression) plus nbhd_cloud/cells/by_gene/available_gene_scatter.json — {gene: max_expression}, the manifest the frontend checks before fetching a gene's cells.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: adata : AnnData Cell-level AnnData with spatial coordinates in obsm["spatial"], a slice_attr (and, if given, z_attr) column in obs, and every gene in gene_list present in adata.var_names. gene_list : Sequence[str] Genes to write a cell scatter for. path_dega_files : str | Path DegaFiles root directory. slice_attr, z_attr : str, str | None See write_meta_slice. min_expression : float A cell counts as "expressing" a gene when its value is at least this. min_cells : int Minimum number of expressing cells (before capping) required to write a gene's scatter at all; genes with fewer are silently skipped. max_cells : int Cap on the number of top-expressing cells written per gene (across all slices combined). progress_every : int Print a progress line every this many genes processed (0 disables).

docs.title: write_nbhd_cloud_cells(adata, path_dega_files, cluster_attr='cluster', slice_attr='slice_id', z_attr=None, max_cells=None, random_state=0)
docs.text:
Write nbhd_cloud/cells/by_cluster/cluster_<id>.parquet, one file per cluster.

Each row: cell_id, x, y, z, cluster_id, slice_id. Cluster selection (not per-neighborhood) is the frontend's cell-display trigger — picking a cluster shows its cells across every slice, optionally narrowed to one slice client-side (the slice_id column is already there) when the slice bar has isolated one slice. A per-cluster file is the natural fit for that: one bounded fetch per selection, not one per slice.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: adata : AnnData Cell-level AnnData with spatial coordinates in obsm["spatial"] and cluster_attr / slice_attr (and, if given, z_attr) columns in obs. path_dega_files : str | Path DegaFiles root directory. cluster_attr, slice_attr, z_attr : str, str, str | None See write_meta_slice. max_cells : int | None Cap on the number of cells written per cluster (across all its slices combined). Above this many, a uniform random subsample is written instead of every cell -- unlike a gene's top-expressing cell cap (max_cells on write_gene_cell_scatter), there's no per-cell ranking signal within a cluster (every member is equally "in" the cluster), so random is the only choice that doesn't bias toward an arbitrary subset. None (default) writes every cell, matching this function's original, uncapped behavior. random_state : int Seed for the subsampling RNG, so results are reproducible run to run.

Needs unique ids (name) and slice_id, cluster_id, color, cell_count columns. path_dega_files : str | Path Output DegaFiles root directory. cluster_attr, slice_attr, z_attr See write_meta_slice / write_nbhd_cloud_cells. max_cells, random_state Forwarded to write_nbhd_cloud_cells — cap (via uniform random subsample) on cells written per cluster. max_cells=None (default) writes every cell, unchanged from this function's original behavior. write_meta_gene : bool Whether to write meta_gene.parquet (the dataset-root per-gene stats). True (default) preserves the original behavior; False skips it for a clusters-only cloud with no gene-expression data.

Write shapes and neighborhood metadata:

  • nbhd_cloud/shapes/by_slice/slice_<id>.parquet — one file per slice, every cluster's polygon, with a geometry_geojson string column (a JSON geometry, e.g. MultiPolygon with XYZ coordinates) rather than GeoParquet/WKB, since it's fed straight into a deck.gl GeoJsonLayer the same way the 2D nbhd feature's GeoJSON already is.
  • nbhd_cloud/meta_neighborhood.parquet — neighborhood_id, cluster_id, slice_id, color, area, cell_count, inv_alpha.
  • cell_clusters/meta_cluster.parquet (via write_cell_clusters_meta).

Per-neighborhood gene expression and population proportions are intentionally not computed/written here: gene coloring comes from the per-gene cell scatter (write_gene_cell_scatter), and population proportions were never surfaced in the frontend.

docs.title: write_point_cloud_dataset(adata, path_dega_files, *, name=None, z_key='Z', cluster_key=None, write_genes=None, write_base_metadata=None, overwrite=False, use_int_index=None, coordinate_resolution=None, compression='snappy', compression_level=None)
docs.text: Write cell positions (and clusters/genes) to a point-cloud DegaFiles.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
adata : AnnData Cell-level AnnData. obsm["spatial"] provides x/y (its first two columns); z is taken from obs[z_key] if present, else from a third spatial column, else 0. Cell names come from obs_names. path_dega_files : str or Path Target point-cloud DegaFiles directory. If it already contains a manifest the writer appends a named position variant; otherwise it creates a fresh point-cloud directory. name : str, optional Name of a position variant (e.g. one alignment of the cells). Positions are written to cell_metadata_<name>.parquet and the name is listed under "alignments" in the manifest; view it with CellCloud(..., alignment="<name>"). Required in append mode. When omitted, only the base cell_metadata.parquet is written. z_key : str, optional, default "Z" obs column holding the z (depth) coordinate. cluster_key : str, optional Only used in create mode: obs column to export as clusters (with colors from uns[f"{cluster_key}_colors"] when available). write_genes : bool, optional Only used in create mode. Whether to export gene expression to cbg/ + meta_gene.parquet (keyed by cell name). Defaults to True when adata carries an expression matrix (layers['counts'] or X). write_base_metadata : bool, optional Whether to also (over)write the base cell_metadata.parquet with these positions. Defaults to True in create mode and False in append mode (so an append never clobbers the existing default positions). overwrite : bool, default False Allow overwriting an existing cell_metadata_<name>.parquet, or an existing dataset when no name is given.

bool, optional

Store original observation IDs once in cell_ids.parquet; use uint32 row positions in geometry, clustering and per-gene files. Defaults to False for a new dataset, or inherits the existing dataset on append. Appending requires exactly the same cells and preserves their original order even when the new AnnData is reordered.

coordinate_resolution : float, optional Round coordinates to this step in their physical units. Use 1.0 for nearest-micron positions (at most 0.5 microns of error on each axis). Integral steps use int32 coordinates; the default keeps float32. An appended alignment inherits the existing resolution. compression : str Parquet compression codec; defaults to "snappy". "zstd" with compression_level=6 provides compact storage. Integer IDs also use delta encoding. compression_level : int, optional Compression level, when supported by the chosen codec.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: pathlib.Path Path to the written positions file (the named variant when name is given, else cell_metadata.parquet).

docs.title: write_point_cloud_zarr(adata, store, *, z_key='Z', cluster_key=None, alignments=None, coordinate_resolution=1.0, obs_columns=None, chunk_rows=262144, expression_chunk_size=262144, overwrite=False)
docs.text:
Write a self-contained CellCloud AnnData Zarr store for HTTP hosting.

X is CSC, so selecting a gene reads only its sparse values and cell-row indices. obs_names retain the original cell IDs; expression is indexed by their zero-based row positions. obsm['spatial'] stores default XYZ coordinates and obsm['spatial_<name>'] stores each named alignment. Pass CellCloud(zarr_url=..., alignment='<name>') to choose one.

Coordinates remain in their physical units. With the default coordinate_resolution=1.0, micron coordinates are rounded to the nearest micron and saved as int32, with at most half a micron of error on each axis. Pass None to retain float32 positions. Original inputs are never modified. A new output path is required unless overwrite=True.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: adata : AnnData Cells, original observation IDs, gene IDs, and counts in layers['counts'] or X. Spatial positions follow the same rules as write_point_cloud_dataset. store : str or Path New local directory; upload its complete contents to a static host. cluster_key : str, optional Cluster observation column. Its palette is retained and missing colors are generated. Other requested observation columns remain available. alignments : mapping of str to array, optional Additional (n_cells, 3) XYZ arrays in exactly adata.obs_names order. These are rounded using the same coordinate resolution. obs_columns : sequence of str, optional Observation columns to keep; defaults to all columns. cluster_key is always retained when provided. chunk_rows : int Number of cells per coordinate chunk (default 262,144). expression_chunk_size : int Number of sparse expression entries per chunk (default 262,144). overwrite : bool Replace an existing local store only when explicitly requested.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: pathlib.Path The completed Zarr v2 store. Numeric arrays use Zstandard compression with bit shuffle; consolidated metadata reduces HTTP round trips.
